chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
The example of seeking forgiveness is like a leaf on a tree that is shaken, so it falls off; and the one who seeks forgiveness from a sin but continues to commit it is like the one mocking his Lord.

key_terms.يَفْعَلُهُ: He commits it (continues to do it)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between true repentance and merely saying 'I seek forgiveness' while continuing to sin?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) employs the vivid metaphor of a leaf shaken from a tree to demonstrate that mere verbal repentance is transient and insufficient if the underlying sin persists. This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *siddqiyyah* (sincerity) and the necessity of behavioral change, warning that hypocrisy in seeking pardon is akin to mocking the Divine. It highlights the critical distinction between superficial ritual and genuine spiritual transformation.
